title: The Moving Drone: Negotiating Agency Between the Voice and the Virtual
abstract: Melodic material in Hindustani music is presented in relation to a tonic, usually sustained by the tanpura, a four-stringed drone instrument. Rooted in Hindustani music, 'The Moving Drone' sets the traditionally static drone into motion that, throughout the performance, gains increasing agency transitioning from reactive to more proactive roles. title: VietFashion: Benchmarking Sketch-Text Composed Image Retrieval for Cultural Outfits
abstract: Cultural garments pose a unique challenge for visual retrieval systems, as their identity often depends on subtle structural and symbolic details that are poorly captured by standard AI models. We introduce VietFashion, a new benchmark for sketch-text composed image retrieval centered on the Ao Dai, a traditional Vietnamese garment. title: Mod-Guide: An LLM-based Content Moderation Feedback System to Address Insensitive Speech toward Indigenous Ethnic and Religious Minority Communities
abstract: Language operates as a mechanism of both marginalization and resistance, especially for minority communities navigating insensitive and harmful speech online. title: Zero-Shot Captioning for Cultural Heritage: Automated Image Analysis of Traditional Indonesian Clothing
abstract: This paper presents Custom ZeroCLIP, a retrieval-augmented vision-language framework for zero-shot captioning of Indonesian traditional garments. The dataset contains 3,800 expert-annotated images from all 38 Indonesian provinces. Using a province-level inductive zero-shot protocol, the model is trained on 24 seen provinces, validated on 6 seen provinces, and evaluated on 8 unseen provinces. title: LAUKIN: A Multi-jurisdictional Common Law Contract Dataset
abstract: Multinational companies increasingly require cross-jurisdictional contract review, yet existing legal NLP datasets are largely restricted to a single jurisdiction. We introduce LAUKIN (Legal equivalence dataset of Australia, UK, and INdia), a dataset of clause pairs (AU-UK, UK-IN, IN-AU) labelled for boolean legal equivalence. title: An Embodied Simulation Platform, Benchmark, and Data-Efficient Augmentation Framework for Wet-Lab Robotics
abstract: Wet-lab robots can improve the reproducibility, throughput, and safety of biomedical experiments, but scaling their learning requires customizable simulators for safe and reproducible task generation, open editable laboratory assets, and efficient pipelines that turn limited demonstrations into usable training data. title: Exploring How Agent Voice Accents Shape Human-AI Collaboration in K-12 Group Learning
abstract: Collaboration is widely recognized as a cornerstone of 21st-century education, yet teachers still encounter persistent challenges in fostering productive peer interaction. LLM conversational peer agents introduce new possibilities for mediating in-person group work, raising questions about how persona design, particularly their voice characteristics, shapes learners' perceptions, trust, and interactional dynamics. title: Finding Conservation Laws of Large Dynamical Systems with Tasks and Futures: A Case Study in Utilizing Dynamic Data Dependencies
abstract: As parallel workloads grow in complexity, managing fine-grained data dependencies becomes a critical challenge. Futures offer a promising model for handling these dependencies, particularly in irregular algorithms, but they also come with the restriction of value-immutability. title: A Declining CVaR Glidepath Framework for Target-Date Fund Design with an Application to the Chilean Pension System
abstract: We propose a framework for designing Target-Date Funds (TDFs) around an explicit return objective while controlling risk directly at the portfolio level through a declining Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) constraint. In this approach, the regulator or sponsor specifies a CVaR glidepath that gives the portfolio manager enough flexibility to reach a target return with a reasonably high probability. title: Diffusive Dynamics of Nonstabilizerness
abstract: Symmetries shape the quantum-information dynamics of many-body systems, but their effect on nonstabilizerness, the resource complementary to entanglement, is less understood. We compute the stabilizer Rényi entropy, a measure of nonstabilizerness, in $\mathrm{U}(1)$-symmetric one-dimensional random circuits. title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Marketplace Feedback for Objective-Weight Adaptation in Three-Sided Dispatch
abstract: Dispatch in three-sided marketplaces provides a natural setting for reinforcement learning from world feedback: decisions are evaluated by delayed operational outcomes such as delivery speed, courier utilization, and merchant congestion. We present a deployed reinforcement learning system at DoorDash that adapts dispatch objective weights in a large-scale food-delivery marketplace using delayed signals. title: CloudCons: A Comprehensive End-to-End Benchmark for Cloud Resource Consolidation
abstract: Driven by conservative over-provisioning to guarantee service reliability, resource utilization in cloud data centers remains at low levels. To mitigate this, the forecast-then-optimize paradigm has emerged to optimize consolidation by anticipating future demands. While emerging time series foundation models promise to enhance this paradigm through zero-shot generalization, existing benchmarks focus solely on prediction error metrics. title: Integrable metrics with potentials on the Hardy space and a class of PDEs
abstract: We introduce a new class of quadratic in the momenta Hamiltonians with potential on Banach spaces of infinite dimension which possess an infinite family of conserved quantities in involution with respect to a naturally defined Poisson structure. title: Representation-Induced Symmetry Trapping in Adaptive Variational Quantum Simulations of Multi-Reference Topologies
abstract: Evaluating the trainability of adaptive quantum chemistry algorithms under multi-reference static correlation requires understanding how representation topologies intertwine with molecular geometry. title: Rarity-Gated Context Conditioning for Offline Imitation Learning-Based Maritime Anomaly Detection
abstract: Contextual anomaly detection aims to identify abnormal behavior conditional on context variables, but practical deployments often face highly imbalanced context distributions where rare regimes can be critical information. Under such frequency bias, context-conditioned models can produce unstable decisions and excessive false alarms in rare contexts. title: Archê, an orbital-free molecular dynamics code for fast production of equations of state
abstract: We present Archê, an orbital-free molecular dynamics (OFMD) code designed to produce equations of state (EOS) in the plasma state. Unlike in other OFMD codes, Archê uses a self-consistent field (SCF) approach to compute the electronic density. This allows us to implement two algorithms that accelerate SCF convergence by a factor of up to six. title: Constrained Semantic Decompression in LLMs through Persian Proverb-Conditioned Story Generation
abstract: Transforming a dense, abstract proverb into an engaging and morally faithful narrative requires deep cultural understanding and robust semantic grounding. We frame this problem as a \emph{constrained semantic decompression} task and study proverb-conditioned story generation as a testbed for abstraction-to-realization in large language models (LLMs). Focusing on Persian, we introduce the Proverb Aligned Narrative Dataset (PAND), pairing proverbs with human-written stories and explicit meanings.

title: Why AI Slop Matters, but Not Like That
abstract: This is a response to the paper ''Why Slop Matters''. By offering both immanent and external critique, we argue that the authors' reasoning neglects the socio-technical context of AI slop. Our paper presents an ethical and social science informed response that centers the debate on the social function and aesthetic value of AI slop. title: A Computational Model for Measuring Adaptability Among U.S. Farmers: Evidence from 1997-2022
abstract: Agricultural crops are a type of cultural trait and the way farmers of US counties select them can itself result in county-level cultural traits. Using real-world data from 1997 to 2022, we have developed a systematic framework to study the selective mechanisms behind these traits. Our findings indicate that environmental payoff-biased selection has driven counties to adopt traits that maximize their adaptability and yield within their specific environments. These empirical results align with ex

title: Illumination-Invariant Anomaly Detection for Sub-Canopy UAV Multispectral Point Clouds
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) multispectral point clouds (MPC) provide high-dimensional spatial-spectral data for sub-canopy target detection; however, their efficacy is significantly compromised by severe illumination heterogeneity caused by vegetation shadows. title: Hydrodynamically engineered Indigenous arrows skip on water for waterfowl hunting
abstract: Across the Northern Hemisphere, Indigenous hunters developed arrows capable of skipping across the water surface to strike waterfowl. Archaeological and ethnographic records reveal remarkably similar projectile designs spanning millennia and geographically distant cultures, suggesting a convergent technological solution. title: Correlated uniform attachment trees
abstract: We introduce and study a new model of correlated uniform attachment (UA) trees, where correlation is sprinkled throughout the time evolution of the process. In this model, two UA trees are grown in parallel, and at each time step a new node is added to each tree, with an edge between it and a uniformly chosen existing vertex in the respective tree. abstract: Purpose: Digitization projects in the humanities produce vast, heterogeneous archives of historical documents, making manual sorting impractical at scale. This work addresses the need for an automated system to classify scanned page images based on visual content type - text, tables, and graphics - enabling content-specific downstream processing such as Optical Character Recognition (OCR) or structured data extraction. title: The Absolute Age of the Open Cluster NGC 6791 and Its Implications for Galactic Archaeology and Asteroseismic Calibration
abstract: We present a new absolute age determination for NGC 6791, one of the Milky Way's oldest and most metal-rich open clusters. Its unusual properties make it an important probe of inner-disk evolution and asteroseismic calibration, but its age has remained difficult to determine because of coupled uncertainties in reddening, distance, photometry, and stellar-model physics. abstract: Theoretical models predict that subgiants within a narrow mass regime can retain detectable lithium enrichment signatures from planetary engulfment. We test this prediction using TOI-5882, selected because it occupies this favorable subgiant parameter space and hosts a massive brown dwarf ($22 \, M_{ \rm J}$, $P=7.1 \,{\rm d}$) companion capable of dynamically perturbing inner planets. abstract: Underwater images suffer from severe wavelength-dependent light absorption and scattering, and turbidity due to suspended particles, degrading visual quality for applications in autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), marine biology, archaeology, and offshore infrastructure inspection. abstract: Jigsaw puzzle solving has been an increasingly popular task in the computer vision research community. Recent works have utilized cutting-edge architectures and computational approaches to reassemble groups of pieces into a coherent image, while achieving increasingly good results on well established datasets. title: Stellar Age Compression Reshapes Interpretations of the Milky Way Thick-Disk Formation History
abstract: The formation timescale of the Milky Way thick disk is one of the central debates in Galactic archaeology. The age-metallicity relation (AMR), formation timescale, and chemical evolution gradients are frequently used to infer a rapid assembly, short-timescale enrichment, and bursty formation history of the thick disk. Deep Learning-Based Automatic Detection of Murals Deterioration: A Case Study of Mogao Grottoes
authors: Zhang Wei, Li Ming, Wang Xiaoming, Chen Jing
abstract: This study proposes a novel deep learning framework for automatic detection and classification of mural deterioration patterns in cave temples. Using high-resolution multispectral images of the Mogao Grottoes, we trained a customized ResNet-152 architecture to identify six types of deterioration including flaking, cracking, salt efflorescence, and pigment fading, achieving an overall F1-score of 0.93. The system can process one square meter of mural surface in approximately 3 seconds, making it suitable for large-scale heritage monitoring applications.

title: 社区参与视角下的传统村落文化遗产活化路径研究——以皖南古村落为例
abstract: 本文以皖南地区西递、宏村等6个传统村落为案例，通过参与式观察与半结构化访谈，探讨社区参与在传统村落文化遗产活化中的角色与机制。研究发现，社区主导型活化模式在文化传承可持续性、居民满意度方面显著优于政府主导型和企业主导型。文章提出「社区赋权-多元共治-利益共享」三阶活化路径框架。

title: Knowledge Graph Construction for Chinese Intangible Cultural Heritage: Method and Application
authors: Li Hua, Zhou Jing, Wu Peng, Yang Fan
abstract: We present a comprehensive knowledge graph for Chinese Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH-KG), integrating data from UNESCO lists, China's national ICH inventory, and local gazetteers. The graph contains over 50,000 entities and 200,000 relations across categories including traditional crafts, performing arts, and oral traditions. We demonstrate its application in ICH discovery, cross-category linkage analysis, and personalized heritage tourism recommendation systems.

title: 从「申遗热」到「后申遗时代」：中国世界遗产管理的制度变迁与挑战
abstract: 本文系统梳理了中国自1985年加入《世界遗产公约》以来40年的遗产管理历程，将其划分为「申遗驱动期」（1985-2004）、「快速增长期」（2005-2019）和「后申遗时代」（2020至今）三个阶段。文章分析了各阶段的制度特征、主要矛盾和典型案例，提出后申遗时代的核心挑战包括：监测体系薄弱、过度旅游化、社区权益保障不足等，并给出政策建议。

title: Multi-Spectral Imaging and Machine Learning for Ancient Bronze Inscription Decipherment
authors: Wang Tao, Liu Yang, Chen Xi, Zhang Lei
abstract: This paper introduces a combined approach using multi-spectral imaging (MSI) and transformer-based machine learning for the decipherment of ancient Chinese bronze inscriptions. The method was tested on 200 artifacts from the Shang and Zhou dynasties, achieving a 34% improvement in character recognition accuracy compared to traditional single-spectrum photography, particularly effective for heavily corroded or worn surfaces.

title: 大运河文化带非物质文化遗产空间分布特征与旅游活化模式研究
authors: 黄丽萍, 孙建国, 朱峰
abstract: 以大运河沿线8省市为研究区域，运用GIS空间分析与地理探测器方法，分析了大运河文化带国家级非遗项目的空间分布特征及其影响因素。结果表明，大运河沿线非遗呈现「核心-边缘」分布格局，北京、苏州、杭州为三大核心集聚区。研究提出「水上非遗走廊」旅游活化概念，并设计了串联38个非遗节点的主题旅游线路。

title: Climate Risk Assessment for UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Southeast Asia: 2025-2050 Projections
authors: Tanawat Chaisuwan, Nguyen Thi Mai, Siti Nurhaliza, David Smith
abstract: This study assesses climate change risks for 44 UNESCO World Heritage sites across Southeast Asia using CMIP6 climate projections under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Key findings include: 62% of coastal heritage sites face high flood risk by 2050, traditional masonry structures show increased weathering rates due to temperature-humidity coupling, and 15 sites may require emergency adaptation measures within the next decade.

title: 甲骨文智能缀合：基于深度度量学习的碎片匹配算法
authors: 杨帆, 张磊, 李想, 王鑫
abstract: 提出了一种基于深度度量学习的甲骨碎片自动缀合算法OracleJoin-Net。通过构建包含15万张甲骨碎片图像的数据集，训练孪生网络学习碎片边缘几何特征与表面纹理特征的联合嵌入空间，实现了碎片对的自动匹配与缀合。实验表明，在Top-10召回率上达到87.3%，成功缀合了12组此前未缀合的甲骨碎片，经古文字学家验证全部正确。

title: OBDC-Unet: a U-shaped network leveraging wavelet dynamics and multi-scale receptive fields for oracle bone drill chisel segmentation
